newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - NI Electric provide for MMC review.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - NI Electric provide for MMC review.

text.p: Northern Ireland Electricity Plc (NIE) has made adequate provisions to cover the effects of price cut recommendations from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), finance director Nigel Wilson said in a telephone interview on Friday.
"We have tried to reflect the severity of the review...our provisions are adequate," he said.
NIE said earlier that exceptional charges of 50.6 million stg brought pretax profits for the year ending March 31 to 59.8 million stg from 107.4 million stg a year ago.
It has accepted a recommendation from the MMC that prices should be cut by 25 percent this year, compared to a cut of 31 percent proposed by its regulator Ofreg.
But Ofreg said there were parts of the MMC's findings which it was "not...currently minded" to accept when they were announced on April 25.
Wilson said NIE had written to Ofreg asking for clarification but was still awaiting a reply and said it was "disappointing" that there had been no meeting.

Wilson said that the "cloud of financial uncertainty" from Ofreg's position and a possible "windfall" tax planned by the new Labour government, NIE was unwilling to give any details on dividend growth or possible share buybacks.
"We shouldn't say more on dividends or share buybacks or capital restructuring...we would have liked to have," he said.

NIE said in its results statement that it was confident of delivering "real dividend growth" and said it would apply to renew its mandate for a buyback of up to 14.9 percent of shares at the annual meeting on July 4.

Wilson said NIE had not made provisions against a possible windfall tax from Labour, because "we don't know what it is, we don't know whether it applies to us...there's too much uncertainty to actually make a provison."
